items.title: Free flu and Covid-19 shots start today in Ontario — are you eligible?
items.summary: Ontario begins free flu and COVID-19 vaccinations for high-risk groups Sept. 28. Most residents can get shots starting Oct. 26; infant RSV immunization starts Oct. 1. The fall flu season is here, and free flu and COVID-19 vaccinations are starting to roll out across Ontario. Free influenza and COVID-19 vaccines are available starting today for high-risk residents across Ontario, while the rest of the province will have to wait another month before they can get the shots to reduce illness. The government of Ontario announced the initial supply of COVID-19 and influenza vaccinations is available this week for hospital staff and patients, residents and staff in long-term-care homes, retirement homes and other congregate living places. Individuals aged 65 and older can also get the free vaccinations starting today, but the availability of vaccines may vary from various health-care providers and pharmacies. The vaccinations are meant to prevent the spread of serious symptoms from the flu, COVID-19 and other respiratory illnesses. According to the government of Canada, flu symptoms generally appear one to four days after exposure to the virus. Symptoms usually include the sudden appearance of fever, cough, muscle aches and pain, and can also include chills, fatigue, sore throat and a runny or stuffy nose. Serious complications and outcomes of the flu can include worsening of chronic health conditions, heart complications, pneumonia and respiratory failure, which could lead to hospitalization or death. The flu is among the 10 leading causes of death in Canada, with 3,500 deaths reported annually.

items.title: Nature’s marathon returns: Watch salmon swim upstream in Mississauga
items.summary: Each fall, salmon travel upstream through the Credit River to spawn. Here's where to spot them and how to respect the run. Every fall, one of nature’s most impressive journeys takes place right here in Mississauga. As the weather cools, thousands of salmon leave Lake Ontario and swim upstream through the Credit River. Guided by instinct, they return to the waters where they were hatched to lay their eggs. The annual salmon migration, often called the salmon run, is one of Mississauga’s most remarkable wildlife events. The salmon run typically begins in September, peaks in early October and continues through the fall, depending on weather and water conditions. Each year, residents head to local parks and trails to watch salmon battle strong currents on their journey home. Whether you’re hoping to snap a photo, enjoy a fall walk or simply witness one of nature’s greatest journeys, the Credit River offers a front-row seat to the salmon run. Just remember to watch respectfully and let the fish finish the race they’ve spent years preparing for. For salmon, fall is more than colourful leaves and cooler weather. It’s time to head home. To give their eggs the best chance at survival, they travel upstream in search of still waters where they can dig their gravel nest, called a redd, to lay their eggs. Salmon begin their migration from Lake Ontario into the Credit River watershed in the fall.

items.summary: The Ontario government announced Monday it is pledging $6 million to combat auto theft, including $300,000 to Peel police.

items.title: Car thefts on the decline in Mississauga and Brampton: Peel police
items.summary: Car thefts are down in Mississauga and Brampton, and Peel’s police chief wants to keep the numbers going in that direction. The number of auto thefts has decreased from 3,089 (Jan. 1, 2025 to June 30, 2025) to 2,790 during the same six-month period in 2026, Peel Regional Police numbers show. “We have made significant steps in addressing the ongoing threat of auto theft in our communities, and it’s critical that we keep our foot on the gas,” Peel police Chief Nishan Duraiappah said Monday. ” Duraiappah’s comments came as he and other Peel officials hosted Ontario Solicitor General Michael Kerzner Monday morning at police headquarters in Mississauga. Kerzner was in town to announce additional provincial funding for Peel Regional Police and other law enforcement agencies across Ontario in the battle against auto theft. “Auto theft is down across Ontario because our government is making it a priority and is giving police the tools and resources they need to go after the organized criminals who are behind it,” said Kerzner. “While we are seeing real progress, we will not let up. ” According to Équité Association’s 2025 auto trend report, vehicle thefts in Ontario declined in 2025 to 19,319, compared to a peak of 30,134 in 2023, a reduction of 36 per cent.

items.title: One card provides endless value at your local library
items.summary: Public libraries help residents cut costs by offering a variety of free entertainment, resources and services. The most valuable card in your wallet could be a library card. As more residents look for ways to save money, find entertainment and connect with their communities, Mississauga Library offers a simple solution: a free library card. Many people think of libraries as places to borrow books, but a library card can open the door to so much more. From books, movies and video games to online learning, career resources, digital news and family activities, it unlocks access to services that might otherwise require subscription fees, making it one of the best values available to residents. Beyond the savings, the real value of a library card isn’t just what you can borrow; it’s the opportunities it creates. Public libraries are welcoming spaces where you can learn, grow, connect and explore. They are a vital part of their communities, where you can learn new skills, attend events, explore interests, build connections, and access supports regardless of age, income or background. Whether you’re looking for your next great read, helping a child discover a love of learning, starting or advancing your career, learning a new language, launching a business, or looking for fun activities, endless opportunities begin at the library. There has never been a better time to sign up for a library card and discover everything Mississauga Library has to offer. Thousands of digital titles available to borrow anytime, anywhere through your library’s digital collection, making it easier and more convenient than ever. Keep up with breaking news stories with access to magazines, newspapers and more trusted news sources from around the world.

items.title: Second Kinton Ramen Location Joins a Wave of New Restaurant Openings Across the Region This September
items.summary: According to insauga.com, a handful of new restaurants opened their doors across Mississauga, Oshawa and Niagara this September, giving local diners fresh options to try. In Mississauga, Japanese ramen chain Kinton Ramen opened a second local location, joining its existing spot on Confederation Parkway near Square One Shopping Centre. The chain specializes in slow-cooked broths served with a variety of noodles and toppings, and has grown from its Toronto roots in 2012 to more than 60 locations across Canada. Elsewhere in the region, Niagara-on-the-Lake gained two new dining spots, Terrain and The Rooftop, both housed inside The Clayfield, a newly opened Hyatt Unbound Collection hotel. Terrain serves as an all-day restaurant built around local food and Niagara wines, with dishes such as East Coast scallop crudo, wild rice risotto, house-made lobster bucatini and dry-aged duck lettuce wraps. The rollout reflects a broader trend of new dining destinations opening across southern Ontario this month, from ramen shops to hotel-anchored restaurants.

items.title: Just Seven of 17 Ward 7 Hopefuls Show Up to Answer Voters' Questions in Mississauga
items.summary: According to a report from mississauga.com, only seven of the seventeen candidates running for Mississauga's Ward 7 council seat turned up for a public meeting where residents could question them directly. The Sept. 14 event, organized by the Applewood Heights and Hills Residents' Association, drew more than 30 attendees to the Royal Canadian Legion branch on Dundas Street. Topics ranged from crime and affordability to concerns over e-scooters in the ward. Adad, a former manager with Safe City Mississauga who spent a decade working in crime prevention and the non-profit sector, told the crowd he wants candidates to move past short-term election promises and focus on longer-term solutions. Alves, a former Peel District School Board trustee, argued that new housing developments in the area have not been planned with Ward 7 families in mind. The low turnout among candidates left many residents' questions unanswered by more than half the field seeking the seat. With the Oct. 26 municipal election approaching, voters looking for direct answers from candidates may need to seek out other forums before voting day.

items.title: Mississauga Opens Early Voting Options Starting Oct. 6 Ahead of Election Day
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, residents wanting to skip the lines on election day can start casting an early ballot on Oct. 6. The first stretch of advance voting, running Oct. 6 to 7, is limited to a single location at the Mississauga Civic Centre on City Centre Drive. Starting Oct. 8, advance polling expands to all 11 ward locations across the city, running through Oct. 11. Voters are not restricted to their own ward during this period and may cast a ballot at any available site. City officials note that this flexibility applies only during the advance voting window, not on election day itself. Voting day proper falls on Oct. 26, when residents must return to their assigned polling location. The expanded advance schedule gives Mississauga voters five extra days beyond election day itself to make their choice known.

items.title: Mayoral Debate Reveals Rare Consensus on a New Parking Garage for Troubled Ridgeway Plaza
items.summary: According to INsauga, the idea of building a four-storey parking garage behind Ridgeway Plaza came up Friday afternoon during Mississauga's first mayoral debate of the election season, held at Sheridan College's Hazel McCallion Campus. A moderator asked the four main candidates what they would do to make the west-end plaza, home to roughly 115 restaurants, more pedestrian and traffic friendly. Incumbent Carolyn Parrish, who won a mayoral byelection in June 2024 after Bonnie Crombie left for provincial politics, pointed to a large plot of land behind the plaza and said a paid parking facility there would pay for itself within three to four years. INsauga reports that while the four candidates, who also included city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, disagreed on most issues during the nearly two-hour debate, they largely agreed on building a new parking garage at Ridgeway Plaza. Crombie, who served as Mississauga's mayor from 2014 to 2024 before leaving to lead the Ontario Liberal Party, told the debate audience she is concerned for residents living near the plaza who have dealt with noise and other problems in recent years.
